author: Dale Roberts
title: Here's my article, The Perfect Portfolio with 2 Tickers . No
text:
Here's my article, The Perfect Portfolio with 2 Tickers . Now keep in mind that this is not a portfolio recommendation but an idea for further evaluation, and an opportunity to observe the effect of longer term treasuries in combination with growth assets. Investors may be able to find their own Perfect Portfolio that might potentially allow them to best reach their goals while investing within their risk tolerance level. Investors, of course, may consider other assets such as Canadian and International holdings when building a Balanced Portfolio.
The Perfect Portfolio is constructed in simple fashion from 2 index ETFs; the Equal Weighted S&P 500 ( RSP ) at 80% and the Longer Term Treasuries ( TLT ) at 20%. Here's how the Perfect Portfolio performed in 2017. Portfolio 1 is the Perfect Portfolio. The returns are courtesy of portfoliovisualizer.com and of course, past performance does not guarantee future returns.
We see that the portfolio had a very strong 2017. Here's how that portfolio would stack up vs. the classic 60/40 Balanced Portfolio of Large Cap Broad Market ( IVV ) and a broad-based bond index ( AGG ).
We see the Perfect Portfolio outperform the classic Balanced Portfolio due to the greater stock component. Of course, the equal weight RSP did underperform the cap weighted IVV in 2017. The cap weighted S&P 500 returns are certainly being led by the largest component such as the FAANG high flyers. Those companies would include Facebook ( FB ), Apple ( AAPL ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Netflix ( NFLX ), and Google ( GOOG ) (NASDAQ: GOOGL ). We can throw in Microsoft ( MSFT ) as well as another mega cap tech giant that is delivering that outperformance. Apple and Microsoft currently rank #1 and #2 as the most valuable companies and hence they carry the greatest weight.
